item.title: In Bayfield County, babies get a $100 head start toward college
item.description: A newborn baby is priceless, of course. But in Bayfield County, you can add $100 to that — thanks to a new program called Saving Early for Educational Dreams, or SEED. It’s a $100 educational savings account for all newborns in the county, plus an additional $100 for families who participate in the WIC program. The post In Bayfield County, babies get a $100 head start toward college appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Wisconsinites can’t keep wild frogs or turtles as pets — or race them — under new rule
item.description: The Wisconsin DNR will no longer allow residents to keep wild frogs and turtles as pets. They can't enter them in any races or contests either. The post Wisconsinites can’t keep wild frogs or turtles as pets — or race them — under new rule appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Company behind Old Wisconsin brand plans $125M expansion in Sheboygan
item.description: The company behind the Old Wisconsin smoked sausage brand is planning a $125 million expansion in Sheboygan, the Wisconsin Economic Development Corp. announced Thursday. The post Company behind Old Wisconsin brand plans $125M expansion in Sheboygan appeared first on WPR.

item.title: RSV cases are down. Health experts are optimistic a new vaccine is behind it
item.description: RSV activity is down for a second winter in a row. Some of the state's top infectious disease experts are cautiously optimistic that access to immunizations are contributing to the declining numbers. The post RSV cases are down. item.title: ‘Portraits of Service’ exhibit highlights Wisconsin veterans and their stories
item.description: James Gill was the photographer on a PBS Wisconsin project that spanned decades, documenting the lives of Wisconsinites who served in the military. Over time, he took portraits of veterans of World War II and wars in Korea and Vietnam. The post ‘Portraits of Service’ exhibit highlights Wisconsin veterans and their stories appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Marquette Poll: Wisconsin voters want lower property taxes vs. more funding for schools
item.description: Wisconsin voters are more concerned with reducing their property taxes than increasing funding for public schools. Voters also say they’re less inclined to support a school referendum. The post Marquette Poll: Wisconsin voters want lower property taxes vs. more funding for schools appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Gov. Tony Evers optimistic about property tax deal, says talks continue
item.description: Gov.
